title: Mihály Hentér to Ferenc Rákóczi II, 8 July 1707

documents.shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15, Caps. D, Fasc. 80, fol. 38

plaintext.source: Contemporary or near-contemporary decipherment written above the cipher lines on MNL OL G 15 Caps. D Fasc. 80 fol. 38; overlooked by DECODE R496, whose inline_plaintext field is false.

transcription.source: Authenticated DECODE full-resolution images IMG_R496_I3689_P1.png and IMG_R496_I3690_P2.png
transcription.notes: The interlinear plaintext recovers the substantive message. Some middle clauses remain palaeographically uncertain where the plaintext hand overlaps cipher characters. Archive rights prohibit republishing the scans.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic substitution written with letters, digits, and graphic signs, with nomenclator elements; the same system occurs in Hentér's fols. 40 and 46.

diacritics.note: Several cipher signs resemble letters or digits distinguished by small strokes; a few are graphic signs not safely representable in ASCII.

system.sibling_key: The same cipher appears in MNL OL G 15 Caps. D Fasc. 80 fols. 40 and 46 (DECODE R533 and R534), both with interlinear plaintext.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear plaintext on the target folio itself; DECODE R496 failed to flag it.

conditions.human_role: Provided authenticated access to the DECODE images.

solution.what: Used the authenticated DECODE session and cookie to retrieve the full-resolution recto and verso of R496 and the sibling records R533 and R534.
Located Benedek Láng's identification of fols. 38, 40, and 46 as Hentér's three 1707 monoalphabetic letters (C.Hen.01-03).
Discovered and read the interlinear Hungarian decipherment on R496, recovering the Belgrade pasha's proposed military support, Hentér's audience negotiations, and the request to free a captive.
Checked the closing formula against R533: wi6xi2i4 = Felséged, with the same substitution recurring across the three Hentér letters.

outcome.notes: The historical decipherment covers the full cipher and makes the message's substance clear. About one fifth of a publication-quality diplomatic transcription remains uncertain because the interlinear hand overlaps the cipher, not because the cryptographic values are unknown.
